definition: A range of values for a population mean, calculated from one random sample by a method that gives an interval containing the true mean for a stated percentage of all such samples; a 95% interval does not mean a 95% chance that this particular interval contains the mean.

A symmetric, bell-shaped distribution with heavier tails than the standard normal, fixed by its degrees of freedom ($n - 1$ for one sample of size $n$); for the mean of a normal population it replaces the normal distribution whenever $\sigma$ is unknown and estimated by $s_{n-1}$, whatever the sample size.
